title: Tamil Star Silambarasan Quits Biryani and Switches to Vegetarian Diet at 43
excerpt: The actor known as Simbu told Tamil newspaper Dinamani that non-vegetarian food left him feeling heavy and bloated, prompting a full dietary shift that has transformed his energy levels.
body:
• Tamil actor Silambarasan TR, 43, has switched from non-vegetarian food to a fully vegetarian diet, telling Dinamani newspaper that biryani left him feeling "heavy and bloated."
  • The actor previously lost up to 30 kilograms during the COVID-19 lockdown by quitting meat, alcohol, and training in Bharatanatyam.
  • A dietitian cautions that vegetarian diets require careful planning to avoid gaps in protein, vitamin B12, iron, and omega-3 fatty acids.
  • Silambarasan is currently filming "Arasan" with director Vetri Maaran and has "STR 50" lined up next.

Biryani Out, Vegetables In

Tamil cinema star Silambarasan TR, popularly known as Simbu, has revealed that he has given up his favourite food — biryani — and switched entirely to a vegetarian diet. The 43-year-old actor told Tamil-language newspaper Dinamani that the change came down to how his body responded to food as he aged.

"My favourite food has always been biryani. But after a certain age, your body doesn't stay the same, no matter what you eat. I was eating non-veg regularly before. But now I have shifted to vegetarian food. When I eat non-veg, I feel heavy and bloated. With vegetarian food, it feels lighter."

— Silambarasan TR, actor

He added a note of pragmatism: "We cannot eat everything we like forever. At some point, we have to be strict."

A Transformation Years in the Making

This is not Silambarasan's first brush with dietary discipline. During the COVID-19 lockdown, the actor publicly acknowledged that he had gained significant weight and embarked on a transformation that became one of Tamil cinema's most talked-about fitness stories.

At his heaviest, Silambarasan was reportedly eating five biryanis a day, according to a transformation video he shared on Instagram. He quit meat and alcohol, began cooking his own vegetarian meals, and took up an intense fitness regimen that started at 4:30 AM daily — walking, weight training, swimming, and cardio. He also learned Bharatanatyam during this period.

The results were dramatic. Various reports place his weight loss between 15 and 30 kilograms. During a 2021 promotional interview for his film Maanaadu in Hyderabad, he reflected on the journey: "I worked hard and reformed myself. I quit drinking and eating non-veg and reduced 27 kilos," he told Telugu media.

What the Experts Say

Dt Amreen Sheikh, chief dietitian at KIMS Hospitals in Thane, told The Indian Express that the body usually adjusts well to a vegetarian transition if planned properly.

"Meat-based meals like biryani are rich in protein, iron, and vitamin B12. When someone switches to a vegetarian diet, these nutrients don't automatically appear on the plate," Sheikh said. "The focus has to shift to lentils, dairy, nuts, seeds, and fortified foods to avoid gaps."

She cautioned against common mistakes in the switch. "One big mistake is replacing meat with only carbohydrates like rice or bread. Another is ignoring protein altogether. Many also overlook micronutrients like B12, iron, and omega-3 fats."

Sheikh emphasised that a vegetarian diet is not automatically healthier. "A vegetarian diet can be nutrient-rich or heavily processed, depending on choices. A well-planned vegetarian diet with whole grains, pulses, vegetables, fruits, and good fats can promote heart health, digestion, and weight management."

What's Next for Silambarasan

On the film front, Silambarasan recently resumed shooting for Arasan, directed by acclaimed filmmaker Vetri Maaran, as confirmed by Cinema Express. He also has STR 50 in the pipeline — a project directed by Desingh Periasamy that will see him play a transgender character for the first time. His most recent release was Mani Ratnam's Thug Life, in which he appeared alongside Kamal Haasan.

For a star who built a reputation partly on his larger-than-life persona and publicly documented struggles with weight and discipline, the dietary shift represents a quieter kind of transformation — one driven less by dramatic reinvention and more by the simple reality of a body at 43 that no longer processes biryani the way it did at 25.
nri_angle: Tamil cinema star Silambarasan's shift to vegetarianism resonates with the broader trend of Indian celebrities embracing plant-based diets, a conversation familiar to diaspora audiences balancing traditional and modern food cultures.
